question: does the counting field hold up on apo-holo pairs that no part of its development could have seen
why_no_read_is_spent: this file builds labels from structures released after CryptoBench's last one and never reads a prediction. CryptoBench's accessions are read as names to exclude, which leaks no performance

externality.temporal: both structures of every pair released after 2024-05-08, the newest release date in CryptoBench
externality.sequence: no accession and no UniRef50 cluster at 50% identity is shared with either CryptoBench fold
externality.order: labels exist before any method is run; the preregistration that fixes the methods refers to this file by hash

choices_that_shrink_the_set.ligand_chemistry: a ligand counts only if CryptoBench accepted that component somewhere in its own dataset, which excludes components new to the PDB since the cutoff and biases the set toward established cofactors and drug-like series
choices_that_shrink_the_set.one_unit_per_cluster: the largest campaign here offers 534 apo chains for one protein; taking one unit per UniRef50 cluster stops any target weighting the set, and discards a great deal of real data
choices_that_shrink_the_set.guard_band: a pair whose pocket moves between 1.5 and 2.5 A is not labelled either way, which removes the borderline cases the recovered pRMSD cannot reproduce and makes this set easier than CryptoBench in that one respect

reading_mmcif_gives_what_reading_pdb_giv.what_is_compared: record type, residue name, chain, residue number, insertion code, atom name and element exactly; coordinates to the tolerance, because .pdb stores three decimals and mmCIF stores more
